title: Carthaginiensis Synodus
author: Incertus
source: Translated by Claude from tmp26.tmp26.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

passages.original: Cypriani ad Jubaianum Graece et Latine hic subjungimus ex Collectione Canonica Joannis Zonarae, monachi, qui fuerat magnus Drun- garius Biglae et primus a secretis imperatoris. Theodorus Balsamon epistolam Cypriani retulit quidem in suam quoque collectionem, sed episcoporum sententias praetermisit et concilii acta. LABB. Η ΕΝ ΚΑΡΧΗΔΟΝΗ ΓΕΝΟΜΕΝΗ ΣΥΝΟΔΟΣ (67) ΗΣ ΕΞΙΙΡΧΕΝ Ο ΜΕΓΑΣ ΚΥΠΡΙΑΝΟΣ ΚΑΙ ΙΕΡΟΜΑΡΤΓΣ ΕΠΙΣΚΟΠΟΣΩΝ ΚΑΡΧΗΛΟΝΟΣ
passages.english: [The letter] of Cyprian to Jubaianus we append here in Greek and Latin from the Canonical Collection of John Zonaras, a monk, who had been Grand Drungarius of the Watch and First Secretary of the emperor. Theodore Balsamon did indeed include Cyprian's letter in his own collection as well, but he passed over the opinions of the bishops and the acts of the council. LABBE. THE SYNOD HELD AT CARTHAGE (67), OVER WHICH PRESIDED THE GREAT CYPRIAN, HIEROMARTYR, BEING BISHOP OF CARTHAGE
passages.notes: The letter's opening word ("epistolam S.") stands in the preceding context, so "[The letter]" is supplied. "Drungarius Biglae" is a Byzantine office, the commander of the imperial watch (the Vigla). The Greek heading has scanning errors: ΕΞΙΙΡΧΕΝ for ΕΞΗΡΧΕΝ, ΙΕΡΟΜΑΡΤΓΣ for ΙΕΡΟΜΑΡΤΥΣ, ΕΠΙΣΚΟΠΟΣΩΝ for ΕΠΙΣΚΟΠΟΣ ΩΝ, and ΚΑΡΧΗΛΟΝΟΣ for ΚΑΡΧΗΔΟΝΟΣ. "(67)" is an editorial note number.

passages.original: Hinc ergo notatur, quod a principio non erat in usu apud omnes hic canon. Nota au- tem, quod Afri dicuntur Carthaginenses. Quia au- tem in nonnullis exemplaribus aperte descriptae inveniuntur 84 episcoporum sententiae, qui in eadem fuerunt opinione cum sancto Cypriano : eramus eas quoque scripturi et interpretaturi : sed quia, ut dictum est, septimus secundae synodi canon alia quaedam constituit ab iis, quae hac praesenti epistola continentur, de haereticis et schismaticis qui ad fidem accedunt, praetermissa est corum expositio.
passages.english: From this, then, it is noted that from the beginning this canon was not in use among all. Note also that the Africans are called Carthaginians. And since in some copies there are found, written out in full, the opinions of 84 bishops who were of the same view as Saint Cyprian, we were going to write these out as well and interpret them. But because, as has been said, the seventh canon of the second synod established certain things different from those contained in this present letter concerning heretics and schismatics who come to the faith, their exposition has been passed over.
passages.notes: "eramus" is evidently "eramus [scripturi]", meaning "we were about to". "corum" is a scanning error for "eorum". The "second synod" is presumably the Second Ecumenical Council (Constantinople, 381).

passages.original: Theognis ab Hippone Regio dixit. Secundum sacramentum Dei ei gratiae coelestis, quam accepimus, baptisma, quod est in Ecclesia sancta novimus.
passages.english: Theognis of Hippo Regius said: In accordance with the sacrament of God and of the heavenly grace which we have received, we recognize [only] the baptism which is in the holy Church.
passages.notes: "ei" is read as "et" (a scanning error). "[only]" is supplied from the sense of the council's position. The Latin says only "we know/recognize the baptism which is in the holy Church."
